rationale: The chosen topology is an inductively degenerated common-source LNA with a tapped inductive load, which provides excellent noise performance due to the low input impedance and high transconductance achievable at 2.44 GHz, while the inductive degeneration enables a wide input match (S11 < -15 dB) by tuning the input reactance. The tapped inductor load (Ld) allows for impedance transformation that enhances gain (S21 > 18 dB) without excessive current draw, and the use of a single inductor in the load path satisfies the inductor budget with room for optimization. The topology avoids floating nodes, uses only one inductor (within the max of 3), and maintains a compact device count suitable for the budget of 16 devices. The structure inherently supports low NF by minimizing input capacitance and leveraging the inductor’s Q for reduced noise figure, while the cascode-free design avoids unnecessary current overhead. This topology is robust against the match-forbidden zone due to its grounded-source input configuration, which avoids the C_gd feedback issues of cascode-based designs.
